newsitem.title: UK: Lira firms on ERM entry, bourses bullish.
newsitem.headline: Lira firms on ERM entry, bourses bullish.

text.p: The Italian lira, buoyed by re-entry into Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM), strengthened on Monday and briefly pushed through its new central parity rate of 990 lire per mark.
European bourses traded bullishly, with Frankfurt and Amsterdam closing floor transactions at record highs. London ended only 19 points short of its intra-day peak on the eve of the British budget.

The lira rallied in reaction to the announcement late on Sunday that it had re-joined the European exchange rate mechanism (ERM), from which it had been ejected in 1992 by a wall of foreign exchange bets against the currency.
After firming early in the day, it passed 990 to trade at 989.80 to the mark by 1600 GMT, although it later fell back below the parity level. Late on Friday in Europe it was quoted at around 999.
"The lira is strengthening. Money is flowing out of the Deutsche mark and this is having an effect on the dollar," said Elizabeth Legge, London-based economist at Bankgesellschaft.
And Roger Francis, senior analyst at IBJ International, commented: "Much of the dollar strength is still part of the lira-ERM effect which has hit the mark."
The dollar edged higher in late European trade, clearing the 1.52 marks barrier

In London leading stocks ended 36 points up as their momentum from Friday's dramatic rise followed through amid subsiding fears of an inflationary budget on Tuesday and after Wall Street nudged through its previous trading high.
The Dow opened weaker but soon continued its rally and was up 28 points at 6,499 when European trading closed.

"If the budget is tight the market will have a good run up to Christmas," one trader said. "Hopefully we will see a wise and prudent budget that will mean interest rates won't have to be used much more to simmer things down," another said.
On Friday the FTSE was propelled back through the key 4,000 level in its biggest one day gain for 16-months caused by a sharp turnaround in sentiment ahead of the budget.

In Frankfurt, German shares ended floor trading at a record high, just below the psychological 2,800 barrier. And in after hours electronic trading the IBIS DAX index also nudged its previous trading peak, although it slipped back to close just below.

The market was boosted by Deutsche Telekom, floated last week in the largest share sale in European history. It was the heaviest-traded stock and ended up three percent as initial profit-taking waned.
German technical analysts said they remained bullish on the market's prospects for the remainder of the year and did not rule out the DAX hitting 3,000 points early in 1997.
On the Paris bourse, French shares headed higher to put on nearly one percent after a climb on Friday of 0.98 percent.
"The market is well supported at these levels. It has good momentum," one broker said.

Fire-hit Eurotunnel, suffered, however, after weekend reports that its re-opening for passenger traffic would miss the lucrative Christmas period, with only freight being allowed through the link for months to come
On the bullion market, gold sank to its lowest level since March 2, 1995 and was pressuring key $375 an ounce support at the afternoon fix, dealers said.

Gold fixed in the afternoon at $375.40 per ounce, up 30 cents from the morning and compared with $377.00 on Friday. The morning fix was the lowest setting since $374.75 in March 1995. It closed in London at a mid-price of $375.05.
"We are at new lows for the year and if it goes beyond $375, it could get very ugly," one dealer said.
CURRENCIES AT 1645 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 112.60 yen and 1.5220 marks against 111.34 yen and 1.5039 marks late on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS - CLOSING INDICES
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares ended 35.9 points higher at 4,054.6.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index finished up 21.67 at 2,277.14.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed up 35.50 at 2,799.19.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $375.05 compared with Friday's close of 377.15. Silver finished at $4.81, down eight cents.
